title: Alleviating the Hubble tension with Torsion Condensation (TorC)
tldr: A gauge-theory extension of gravity with a torsion field speeds up early expansion, letting the CMB accept a higher H₀ and removing the Planck–SH0ES tension, though the Bayesian evidence doesn't prefer it over ΛCDM.
newcomer: This paper joins three fields: cosmology (how the Universe expands and what the CMB tells us), gravitational theory (building gravity as a gauge theory, which brings in torsion), and Bayesian statistics (comparing models by their evidence). Each part of the argument leans on a different one.

sections.name: Basics used throughout
sections.summary: Cosmology's starting points: an expanding universe described by general relativity and the ΛCDM recipe.
sections.role: Needed to read any equation, parameter or plot in the paper.

sections.name: The Hubble tension
sections.summary: Early-Universe (CMB) and late-Universe (distance ladder) measurements disagree on how fast the Universe expands today.
sections.role: The problem TorC is tested against, and the data it is fitted to.

sections.name: Gravity as a gauge theory
sections.summary: Building gravity like the other forces, by gauging a symmetry, brings in torsion as a new field.
sections.role: Where TorC comes from: a ghost-free Poincaré gauge theory whose torsion condenses into GR.

sections.name: TorC cosmology
sections.summary: What torsion does to the expansion history: extra early radiation, recast as an effective dark-energy fluid.
sections.role: How the theory is turned into something a Boltzmann code and the data can test.

sections.name: Boltzmann codes and perturbations
sections.summary: Computing CMB spectra from a model needs a Boltzmann code and perturbation theory.
sections.role: A modified CAMB produces TorC's predictions; missing TorC perturbations are the main caveat.

sections.name: Bayesian model comparison
sections.summary: Fitting models, comparing them with the Bayesian evidence, and measuring tension between datasets.
sections.role: Gives the headline numbers: log R for the tension and Δlog Z for TorC versus ΛCDM.

concepts.name: Expanding universe and H₀
concepts.plain: Galaxies recede from us faster the further away they are; the Hubble constant H₀ is today's expansion rate, in km/s per megaparsec.
concepts.why_here: The whole paper is about what value H₀ has.

concepts.name: General relativity
concepts.plain: Einstein's theory: gravity is the curvature of spacetime, set by the matter and energy in it.
concepts.why_here: TorC is an extension of GR, and reduces to it when torsion condenses.

concepts.name: Friedmann equations and ΛCDM
concepts.plain: Applying GR to a uniform universe gives the Friedmann equations, which say how fast space expands given its contents. ΛCDM is the standard recipe: cold dark matter, ordinary matter, radiation and a cosmological constant Λ.
concepts.why_here: ΛCDM is the model TorC is compared against, and TorC contains it as a special case (ϖᵣ = 1).

concepts.name: Density, pressure and w
concepts.plain: Each ingredient of the universe has an energy density ρ and pressure P; their ratio w = P/ρ sets how it dilutes as space expands (radiation w = 1/3, matter 0, Λ −1).
concepts.why_here: Torsion is recast as a dark-energy fluid with its own ρ(a) and P(a), and early on it behaves like radiation (w = 1/3).

concepts.name: The distance ladder (SH0ES)
concepts.plain: Local H₀ comes from a chain of distance indicators: parallaxes calibrate Cepheid stars, Cepheids calibrate type Ia supernovae, and supernovae reach far enough to see the expansion. The tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) is an alternative rung.
concepts.why_here: SH0ES gives H₀ = 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc, the late-Universe side of the tension.

concepts.name: CMB power spectrum
concepts.plain: The cosmic microwave background is light from 380,000 years after the Big Bang. Its temperature and polarisation ripples (TT, TE, EE) show a series of acoustic peaks whose positions and heights encode the cosmological parameters.
concepts.why_here: Planck's CMB data are the early-Universe side of the tension, and the main data TorC is fitted to.

concepts.name: Sound horizon
concepts.plain: Before the CMB was released, sound waves crossed the hot plasma; the distance they travelled (the sound horizon, ~150 Mpc) is a standard ruler. The CMB measures its angle on the sky, so a smaller ruler means a closer CMB and a higher H₀.
concepts.why_here: This is TorC's lever: torsion speeds early expansion, shrinks the sound horizon and lets H₀ rise.

concepts.name: The Hubble tension
concepts.plain: CMB data analysed with ΛCDM predict H₀ ≈ 67 km/s/Mpc, while the local distance ladder measures ≈ 73; the gap is about 5σ.
concepts.why_here: The problem the paper sets out to address.

concepts.name: Early dark energy
concepts.plain: A proposed fix: an extra energy component that matters briefly before recombination, speeding up expansion and shrinking the sound horizon.
concepts.why_here: TorC pulls the same lever as early dark energy, but with an extra field that comes from the structure of gravity rather than being added by hand.

concepts.name: S₈ and cosmic shear
concepts.plain: S₈ measures how clumpy matter is today. Weak-lensing surveys such as KiDS measure it from the distortion of galaxy shapes; some found lower values than Planck.
concepts.why_here: TorC allows lower S₈, but the paper flags this as unreliable without TorC perturbations.

concepts.name: BAO and DESI
concepts.plain: The same sound waves leave a preferred separation between galaxies (baryon acoustic oscillations), measured by surveys like DESI as a ruler at later times.
concepts.why_here: Adding DESI BAO data is listed as the next step.

concepts.name: Gauge theories
concepts.plain: In the Standard Model, forces arise by demanding that physics stays the same under symmetry transformations made differently at each point (local symmetry); each such symmetry brings a force-carrying field.
concepts.why_here: Gravity isn't yet built this way; gauging the Poincaré group is the motivation for TorC.

concepts.name: Tetrads and the spin connection
concepts.plain: An alternative way to describe spacetime with a local set of axes (tetrad) at each point and a spin connection that relates neighbouring axes; with torsion allowed this is Einstein–Cartan theory.
concepts.why_here: These are the gauge fields of Poincaré gauge theory, the variables TorC is built from.

concepts.name: Torsion
concepts.plain: A second way spacetime can be shaped besides curvature: a twisting, so that infinitesimal parallelograms fail to close. GR sets it to zero; other theories let it be a field of its own.
concepts.why_here: TorC's extra degrees of freedom are torsion.

concepts.name: Poincaré gauge theory
concepts.plain: Gravity built as a gauge theory of the Poincaré group (translations and Lorentz rotations), with both curvature and torsion dynamical.
concepts.why_here: TorC is one Poincaré gauge theory, picked from a catalogue of healthy ones.

concepts.name: Ghosts, tachyons and particle spectra
concepts.plain: A healthy theory must not contain ghosts (negative-energy modes) or tachyons (faster-than-light modes); the particle spectrum around a background tells you whether it does.
concepts.why_here: TorC comes from a ghost- and tachyon-free catalogue, but those checks hold only around zero torsion, which the paper lists as an open caveat.

concepts.name: Scalar–tensor theories (Horndeski)
concepts.plain: Theories that add scalar fields to gravity; Horndeski's is the most general with second-order equations, so it stays free of the Ostrogradsky ghost.
concepts.why_here: In a uniform universe TorC's torsion reduces to two scalar fields, which makes its cosmology tractable.

concepts.name: Torsion condensation (TorC)
concepts.plain: A Poincaré gauge theory in which the torsion field condenses to a value of order the Planck mass; the Einstein–Hilbert term of GR then emerges rather than being put in by hand.
concepts.why_here: The theory being tested.

concepts.name: Torsion as dark radiation
concepts.plain: When the torsion field starts away from its ΛCDM value (ϖᵣ < 1), it behaves like extra radiation in the early Universe.
concepts.why_here: This is what speeds early expansion and lets H₀ rise.

concepts.name: Torsion as effective dark energy in CAMB
concepts.plain: The torsion terms in the Friedmann equations are rewritten as a time-varying dark-energy density ρ(a) and pressure P(a), tabulated and fed to the Boltzmann code. Using ρ and P directly avoids the poles that w = P/ρ would have.
concepts.why_here: This implementation is the paper's own technical step, letting the full (ΩΛ, ϖᵣ) space be fitted to Planck.

concepts.name: Big Bang nucleosynthesis and N_eff
concepts.plain: In the first minutes, light elements formed; how much helium appears depends on the expansion rate, often expressed as an effective number of neutrino species N_eff.
concepts.why_here: Torsion's extra early radiation shifts N_eff; the appendix checks this doesn't change the conclusions.

concepts.name: Boltzmann codes (CAMB)
concepts.plain: Programs that evolve the universe's ingredients and their perturbations to predict the CMB and matter power spectra for given parameters.
concepts.why_here: A modified CAMB computes TorC's CMB spectra.

concepts.name: Cosmological perturbation theory
concepts.plain: The theory of small ripples on the uniform background: how density and metric fluctuations grow and imprint the CMB and large-scale structure.
concepts.why_here: TorC's perturbations aren't worked out yet, so the paper keeps ΛCDM's: the main caveat.

concepts.name: Bayesian inference
concepts.plain: Updating beliefs with data: the posterior probability of parameters is the likelihood of the data times the prior, normalised.
concepts.why_here: All constraints are Bayesian posteriors with stated priors.

concepts.name: Nested sampling (PolyChord)
concepts.plain: An algorithm that shrinks a cloud of 'live points' through nested likelihood contours, giving both posterior samples and the Bayesian evidence.
concepts.why_here: PolyChord, run through Cobaya with 1000 live points, does every fit here.

concepts.name: Bayesian evidence and Occam's razor
concepts.plain: The evidence Z is the probability of the data under a model, averaged over its prior. It rewards fit but penalises extra parameters (log Z = fit − Kullback–Leibler 'Occam penalty').
concepts.why_here: Δlog Z decides whether TorC beats ΛCDM: the fit gain of +6.8 is almost cancelled by a penalty of −6.1.

concepts.name: Tension statistics (R)
concepts.plain: The R-statistic compares the evidence for two datasets fitted together with fitting them separately; log R < 0 signals tension.
concepts.why_here: Shows Planck and SH0ES go from strong tension in ΛCDM (log R = −5.6) to consistent in TorC (+0.7).
